---
title: "Parameters"
---

EvoDAG is configured with the arguments of the scikit-learn classes (`EvoDAGClassifier`, `EvoDAGRegressor`, see [Python](python.qmd)), with keyword arguments to its native classes `EvoDAGE`, `EvoDAG.model.EvoDAG` and `RGP.init` (see [Native API](native-api.qmd)), and, as a JSON object, with `EvoDAG-train --kw`. This page starts with what the defaults are and where they come from, and then lists every parameter, what it does and the value it has in the default configuration. For the meaning of terms such as the validation split or the early stopping individual see [How it works](how-it-works.qmd).

## What are EvoDAG's defaults?

The default configuration is what you get from `EvoDAGClassifier()` and `EnsembleClassifier()` (and, for regression, from `EvoDAGRegressor()` and `EnsembleRegressor()`), and from their native counterparts `EvoDAGE()`, `EvoDAG.model.EvoDAG()`, `RGP.init()` and `EvoDAG-train -C`, without saying anything else. For classification it is this:

| | Default |
|:---------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Function set | `Add` 60 arguments, `Mul` 20, `Min` 5, `Max` 5, `Hypot` 2, `NaiveBayes` 5, `NaiveBayesMN` 5, `Centroid` 2, and the one-argument `Fabs`, `Sqrt`, `Sin`, `Tan`, `Atan`, `Tanh` |
| Population | `popsize` 4000, `population_class` `"SteadyState"` |
| Stopping | `early_stopping_rounds` 4000; `time_limit` 3600 seconds for one model, none for an ensemble |
| Validation split | `tr_fraction` 0.5 |
| Fitness | `fitness_function` `"macro-F1"` (the macro-averaged F1 score) |
| Selection of the arguments | the agreement heuristic of the selection paper (`selection` `"agreement"`, `first_selection` `"random"`, `heuristic_functions` `"tailored"`): for `Add`, `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` and `Centroid` the first argument is drawn at random and each other argument is, among `tournament_size` (2) individuals drawn at random, the one whose predicted labels agree least with the first; the arguments of the other functions are drawn at random |
| Selection of the individual that leaves | random (`negative_selection` false) |
| Ensemble (`EnsembleClassifier`, `EvoDAGE`) | `n_estimators` 30, seeds 0 to 29 |

Regression has its own file with a different function set (no `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` or `Centroid`), the fitness `"ER"`, which has no effect there, and the ordinary selections: the file has no selection key, so the arguments are chosen by a tournament on fitness and the individual that leaves by a negative tournament (`negative_selection` true).

### Where they come from

The second EvoDAG paper (see [Citing](citing.qmd)) reports that the default parameters, the number of arguments of each function included, were found by a random search over the parameter space on a benchmark of classification problems (several sentiment analysis problems and problems from the UCI repository, not the ones used to measure the selection heuristics), and that the values kept are the consensus of the parameters that obtained the best performance. The function set, the population size, the early stopping, the validation split and the ensemble size above are those that the paper describes for the system it evaluates.

The paper's best-ranked configuration for the selection is agreement for the parents together with a random choice of the individual that leaves (it is called `agr-rnd` there; see [Selection](selection.qmd)), and it is statistically better than the classical selection, a tournament on fitness for both the parents and the individual that leaves (`fit-fit` there). Since this release (0.19) the classification defaults are the paper's `agr-rnd` configuration as a whole: agreement with a random reference for the four functions, random arguments for the others, a random choice of the individual that leaves and macro-F1 as fitness. **Earlier releases (0.18 and before) used the classical selection and the balanced error rate as fitness**, so a model trained now with the defaults is not the model an earlier release produced.

### What still differs from the paper's setup

* **The first individual is the first argument**, as the paper describes; a winner that repeats an argument is drawn again up to three times and then dropped, so a function receives up to its number of arguments. (Up to version 0.18, and in the program that produced the paper's results, the first individual was left out of the arguments; see [Selection](selection.qmd).)
* **Time limit.** A single model stops after `time_limit` (3600 seconds); the paper has no time limit. An ensemble (`EvoDAGE`, `EnsembleClassifier`) has none unless it is given.
* **Prediction of the ensemble.** The paper says the prediction is the average of the models; `predict` of `EvoDAGE` is the majority vote and `decision_function` is the median.
* **Coefficients.** The coefficients of a node are fitted on a random subsample of the training part (see [How it works](how-it-works.qmd)); the paper says the training set.

There are other, smaller differences that are listed in [How it works](how-it-works.qmd) and in [Selection](selection.qmd).

### The parameters of the scikit-learn classes

`EvoDAGClassifier` and `EvoDAGRegressor` have the arguments `popsize`, `early_stopping_rounds`, `time_limit`, `random_state`, `params_fname` and `params`. `None` in the first three means the value of the JSON file of the defaults (the classification or the regression one, according to the class), so the tables below apply as they are. `random_state` is the `seed` of the engine (an integer, `0` by default). `params` is a dictionary with any other parameter of this page, the function names included: it is where, for example, `selection` or `fitness_function` go. The ensembles (`EnsembleClassifier`, `EnsembleRegressor`) take the estimator, so its parameters are reached with the prefix `estimator__`, and they add `n_estimators` (30), `n_jobs` (1) and, for the classifier, `voting`.

### Getting the classical selection

```python
from EvoDAG import EvoDAGClassifier

# the classical selection: fitness tournaments for the parents and for the
# individual that leaves (the fit-fit of the selection paper)
classic = EvoDAGClassifier(params={"selection": "fitness",
                                   "negative_selection": True})

# the legacy form of the agreement: the first argument and the functions
# without the heuristic are chosen by the tournament on fitness
legacy = EvoDAGClassifier(params={"selection": None,
                                  "orthogonal_selection": True,
                                  "negative_selection": False})
```

The native form is the same keywords given to `EvoDAGE(...)`; on the command line, `EvoDAG-train -C --kw '{"selection": "fitness", "negative_selection": true}'`.

Releases up to 0.18 used the classical selection with the balanced error rate as fitness; since this release the fitness is macro-F1 in every default, as in the selection paper.

### Two layers of defaults

There are two sets of default values and they differ.

1. **The configuration files** `EvoDAG/conf/default_parameters.json`
   (classification) and `EvoDAG/conf/default_parameters_r.json` (regression),
   the ones described above. They are read by the scikit-learn classes,
   `EvoDAGE`, `EvoDAG.model.EvoDAG`, `EvoDAG.EvoDAG.init` (also `RGP.init`) and the command
   line.
2. **The keyword defaults of the constructor of the engine** (`EvoDAG.EvoDAG`, also `RGP` and `RootGP`, in `EvoDAG/base.py`). They apply only when the class is called directly, as in `RGP(...)`, without `init`.

| Parameter | Configuration file (classification) | Constructor of the engine |
|:----------------------|:------------------------|:-------------------------|
| `popsize` | 4000 | 10000 |
| `early_stopping_rounds` | 4000 | -1 (the population size) |
| `function_set` | the 14 functions of the table above | all the functions of `EvoDAG.node` |
| `selection` | `"agreement"` | `None` |
| `negative_selection` | false | true |
| `unique_individuals` | false | true |
| `pr_variable` | 0.9 | 0.33 |
| `all_inputs` | true | false |
| `use_all_vars_input_functions` | true | false |
| `input_functions` | `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN`, `Centroid` | none |
| `time_limit` | 3600 | none |

The two coincide in `tournament_size`, `fs_tournament_size`, `tr_fraction`, `fitness_function`, `random_generations`, `first_selection`, `heuristic_functions`, `min_density`, `finite`, `seed` and `population_class`. Use `init` unless you want the constructor's own values.

A parameters file replaces the default file; it is not merged with it. A file written by `EvoDAG-params` of this release contains the selection keys (`selection`, `first_selection`, `heuristic_functions`, `negative_selection`) and `fitness_function`; a file written by an earlier release has neither the selection keys nor macro-F1, so a model trained from it (`-P`, or `params_fname`) uses the constructor's values for the selection (the tournaments on fitness) and the fitness the file has.

## Where the values come from

When you create a model, its parameters are taken from three places, each one overriding the previous:

1. the default configuration, a JSON file inside the package: `default_parameters.json` for classification and `default_parameters_r.json` for regression (`classifier=False`);
2. a JSON file of your own, if you pass `params_fname` (or `-P` on the command line). It can be a single object, or a list of objects as the one written by `EvoDAG-params`, in which case the first one is used; it replaces the default file;
3. the keyword arguments of the call (in the scikit-learn classes, the arguments `popsize`, `early_stopping_rounds` and `time_limit`, and the dictionary `params`).

Keep in mind two exceptions. `EvoDAGE` has its own `time_limit` argument, which is `None` (no limit) unless you set it, and which replaces the `time_limit` of the file; a single model uses the one in the file (and so does `EvoDAGClassifier`, unless you give its `time_limit`). And the function parameters (below) are not passed one by one to the engine: they are
converted into its function set.

The values in the tables that follow are those of `default_parameters.json`, the classification configuration. Where `default_parameters_r.json` differs it is said.

## The function set

There is one parameter for every function that EvoDAG can use to build an individual. They are written with the name of the function, capitalised. A boolean switches the function on or off; an integer gives the number of arguments that the function takes (a function that takes several arguments uses *up to* that many) and `0` switches it off.

| Function | Meaning | Default |
|:-------------|:-----------------------------------------|:-------------------|
| `Add` | sum of its arguments, with least-squares coefficients | 60 arguments |
| `Mul` | product of its arguments | 20 |
| `Min`, `Max` | element-wise minimum, maximum of the arguments | 5 each |
| `Hypot` | $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$ of two arguments | 2 |
| `Atan2`, `Div` | arctangent of the quotient, and quotient, of two arguments | `Atan2` 0, `Div` false |
| `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` | Gaussian and multinomial Naive Bayes over the arguments (classification only) | 5 each |
| `Centroid` | nearest centroid over the arguments (classification only) | 2 (0 in regression) |
| `Atan`, `Fabs`, `Sin`, `Sqrt`, `Tan`, `Tanh` | one-argument functions | true |
| `Acos`, `Acosh`, `Asin`, `Asinh`, `Atanh`, `Ceil`, `Cos`, `Cosh`, `Exp`, `Expm1`, `Floor`, `Lgamma`, `Log`, `Log10`, `Log1p`, `Log2`, `Sign`, `Sinh`, `Sq` | one-argument functions | false |
| `Argmax`, `Argmin` | present in the file with value 0, but not part of the engine's function set, so a value has no effect | 0 |

In regression `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` and `Centroid` are not used, and in
the regression configuration they are 0.

## Parameters of the evolution

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| `popsize` | 4000 | number of individuals in the population |
| `population_class` | `"SteadyState"` | `"SteadyState"` replaces one individual per step; `"Generational"` replaces the whole population every `popsize` offspring |
| `early_stopping_rounds` | 4000 | the run stops when this many offspring have been created without improving the early stopping individual; a negative value means `popsize` |
| `generations` | `null` | maximum number of generations (a generation is `popsize` offspring); `null` means no limit, and then the early stopping or the time limit ends the run |
| `time_limit` | 3600 | seconds. In an ensemble the limit is shared by all members: a member that finds less than two seconds left is not trained |
| `seed` | 0 | seed of the pseudo-random numbers; the members of an ensemble use `seed`, `seed + 1`, and so on |
| `tournament_size` | 2 | individuals drawn in each tournament, both when selecting arguments and when selecting the one that leaves |
| `random_generations` | 0 | number of generations in which arguments are drawn uniformly instead of by tournament on fitness. It has no effect with the default selection, which does not use a tournament on fitness for the arguments. |
| `selection` | `"agreement"` (not set in regression) | the scheme that chooses the arguments of an offspring: `"fitness"`, `"random"`, `"agreement"`, `"cosine"`, `"pearson"`, `"angle"` or `"novelty"` (see [Selection](selection.qmd)); `None` keeps the behaviour of `orthogonal_selection` and `orthogonal_dot_selection`, which `selection` overrides when it is given. The regression file does not have the key, and then the arguments are chosen by the tournament on fitness. |
| `first_selection` | `"random"` (not set in regression) | how the reference individual of the heuristics `"agreement"`, `"cosine"`, `"pearson"` and `"angle"` is chosen: `"random"` or `"fitness"` |
| `heuristic_functions` | `"tailored"` (not set in regression) | `"tailored"` applies the heuristic only to `Add`, `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` and `Centroid`; `"all"` to every function with more than one argument |
| `negative_selection` | false (true in regression) | when true the individual that an offspring replaces is the worst of a tournament of `tournament_size`; when false it is chosen at random |
| `unique_individuals` | false | when true an offspring that repeats a function applied to the same arguments is rejected |
| `function_selection` | true | when true the function of each offspring is chosen by a tournament on the average fitness its offspring obtained; when false, uniformly at random |
| `fs_tournament_size` | 2 | size of that tournament over functions |
| `min_density` | 0.8 | when the average fraction of non-zero values in the population is below it, only the functions that keep sparse data sparse are used |

## Parameters of the data and the fitness

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| `classifier` | true | classification when true, regression when false |
| `fitness_function` | `"macro-F1"` (`"ER"` in regression, where it has no effect) | measure of the fitness in classification; see below |
| `multiple_outputs` | true | whether the individuals have several outputs. It is always on in classification, where there is one output per class; in regression it is for problems with several targets, and the default configuration for regression turns it off |
| `tr_fraction` | 0.5 | proportion used for training when the data are split into the training and the validation part; see [How it works](how-it-works.qmd#early-stopping-and-the-validation-split). With `1` there is no validation set and `generations` must be set |
| `finite` | true | non-finite values (`nan`, infinities) in the input variables are replaced by zero |

`fitness_function` accepts, for classification: `macro-F1` (the default), `BER` (the mean recall over the classes), `ER` and `accuracy`, `macro-Precision`, `F1` (of one class; the smallest one unless `F1_index` is given), `macro-RecallF1`, `accDotMacroF1`, and variants built from recall, precision and F1 whose names start with `Dot` or `g_` (the geometric mean over the classes) or with `a_` (the arithmetic mean). The definitions are in `EvoDAG/bagging_fitness.py` and `EvoDAG/cython_utils.pyx`. In regression the fitness is always minus the sum of absolute errors on the training part, and the validation fitness the negative relative squared error.

## Parameters of the initial population

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| `all_inputs` | true | create individuals until every input variable has been used once, instead of until the population has `popsize` individuals |
| `pr_variable` | 0.9 | probability that an initial individual is a single input variable rather than an input function over several variables |
| `input_functions` | `["NaiveBayes", "NaiveBayesMN", "Centroid"]` (`null` in regression) | functions used to build the initial individuals that combine inputs; names of functions among `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN`, `Centroid` and `MultipleVariables` (all four at most) |
| `use_all_vars_input_functions` | true | first create one individual for each input function applied to all the variables |
| `share_inputs` | false | has no effect in this release: the lists of inputs that it is meant to share are rebuilt right after |

## Other parameters of the engine

These are not in the default configuration files, but they are accepted by the constructors.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| `orthogonal_selection` | false | the legacy form of the agreement heuristic (the first argument and the functions without the heuristic are chosen by the tournament on fitness; see [Selection](selection.qmd)); it is used only when `selection` is `None` |
| `orthogonal_dot_selection` | false | choose the arguments by a dot-product measure (see [Selection](selection.qmd)) |
| `F1_index` | -1 | class used by `fitness_function="F1"`; -1 means the smallest class |
| `remove_raw_inputs` | true | free the training inputs once the initial population exists |
| `number_tries_feasible_ind` | 30 | attempts to find a valid individual before giving up |
| `probability_calibration` | `None` | a class with the `fit` / `predict_proba` interface of scikit-learn; it is fitted on the outputs of the early stopping individual on the validation part, and then enables `predict_proba` of a single model and the calibrated probabilities of the ensemble |
| `labels` | `None` | the class labels, if you do not want them taken from `y` |
| `max_training_size` | not set | with `n_jobs` greater than 1, each member of the ensemble learns from a random subsample of at most this many examples |

`EvoDAGE` also takes `n_estimators` (30), `n_jobs` (1), `tmpdir` (a directory where finished members are stored, so that an interrupted fit can be resumed) and `time_limit`.

## The random search of parameters

`EvoDAG-params` samples configurations from `parameter_values.json`. It is a JSON object that gives, for each parameter, the list of values that the search may choose from; one configuration takes one value of each list, and the configurations are drawn at random without repetition. The sets are:

| Parameter | Values that the search may choose |
|:--------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------|
| `Add` | 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 |
| `Mul`, `Max`, `Min`, `NaiveBayes`, `Centroid` | 0, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 |
| `NaiveBayesMN` | 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 |
| `Hypot`, `Atan2` | 0, 2 |
| `Acos`, `Asin`, `Atan`, `Cos`, `Div`, `Expm1`, `Fabs`, `Log1p`, `Sin`, `Sq`, `Sqrt`, `Tan` | true, false |
| every other function | false |
| `popsize` | 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 (only those that do not exceed the size of the training set) |
| `early_stopping_rounds` | 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 |
| `population_class` | `"SteadyState"`, `"Generational"` |
| `unique_individuals`, `function_selection`, `all_inputs`, `use_all_vars_input_functions` | true, false |
| `random_generations` | 0, 1 |
| `input_functions` | four lists: all three of `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` and `MultipleVariables`, and each of those alone |
| `selection` | `"agreement"` |
| `first_selection` | `"random"` |
| `heuristic_functions` | `"tailored"` |
| `negative_selection` | false |
| `classifier`, `finite`, `fitness_function`, `fs_tournament_size`, `generations`, `min_density`, `multiple_outputs`, `pr_variable`, `share_inputs`, `time_limit`, `tournament_size`, `tr_fraction` | one fixed value |

In a search for regression (`EvoDAG-params -R`) the four selection parameters (`selection`, `first_selection`, `heuristic_functions` and `negative_selection`) are left out, since agreement with random negative selection is the default of classification only, and the regression search keeps sampling with the constructor's values for them. Combinations that make no sense are skipped: a `Generational` population needs `early_stopping_rounds` at least equal to `popsize`, and `early_stopping_rounds` cannot exceed the number of training examples. Each sampled configuration is trained three times, with seeds 0, 1 and 2, and the configurations are ranked by the median validation fitness of the three runs. See [Command line](cli.qmd) for the options of `EvoDAG-params`, and use `--parameters-values` to search a space of your own.
